name: יְשֻׁרוּן
summary: A poetic name of Israel, four times: in the song of Moses, where “Jeshurun grew fat and kicked” and forsook the God who made him (Deu 32:15); in his blessing, where Yahweh “was king in Jeshurun” when the tribes of Israel gathered, and “there is none like the God of Jeshurun” (Deu 33:5, 26); and in Isaiah, beside Jacob, “Jacob my servant, and Jeshurun whom I have chosen” (Isa 44:2). It is the adjective יָשָׁר “upright” with the ending ‑ûn: Israel called by what it was chosen to be, as Balaam called Israel “the upright” (Num 23:10). Set beside “Jacob”, and in Deu 32:15 against a people that grew fat and turned away, the name holds Israel to its calling; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Jeshurun grew fat and kicked … and forsook God who made him, and scorned the Rock of his salvation.”
“He was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.”
“There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to your help.”
“Do not fear, Jacob my servant, and Jeshurun whom I have chosen.”
Balaam of Israel: “Let me die the death of the upright (יְשָׁרִים).”
In the same song Yahweh is “righteous and upright (יָשָׁר)”, and his people are “a crooked and twisted generation” (v. 5).

note: Takes j.dz.af (4 tokens). TIPNR has no record for the nation and carries Jeshurun as a form of Israel@Gen.25.26 (Jacob), which is tagged here as in names/yisrael. Whether the ending ‑ûn is a diminutive or affectionate ending is not settled by any verse. The Septuagint renders the name ἠγαπημένος “beloved” at each place, a translator's reading and no evidence of the Hebrew.
